Checking the commit hashes to verify the deployment state — the ledger commit 141e3c0f is HEAD and deployed, which is correct since it came after the dashboard commit b0900387. Now I need to build out the QA schedule.

I'm setting up an in-process scheduler in the backend that runs health probes every 5 minutes, auth probes every 15 minutes, and a full matrix every 2 hours. I should check if I can reuse the probe logic from the guardian module rather than duplicating it — let me examine that file to see what functions are available.

I need to set up a QA scheduler backend module that runs on an interval and reuses the guardian probes. The challenge is that guardian doesn't currently export the functions I need, so I'll add those exports and import them into the new scheduler file rather than duplicating code. The guardian file is small enough that this approach works fine.

For the scheduler itself, I'm designing `startAutonomousQAScheduler()` as an idempotent function that kicks off three intervals: a health check every 5 minutes, full auth probes every 15 minutes, and a complete matrix run every 2 hours. I'll persist the scheduler state to a JSON file tracking when each probe last ran, along with counters and a ring buffer of recent results. When a probe failure opens a new incident that's ready for SMS, I'll automatically send an alert using the same SMS logic from guardian, but only on the first occurrence to avoid spam. Finally, I need an owner-only status endpoint at GET /api/ivx/autonomous/qa that exposes the scheduler's current state and recent activity.

To wire this up, I'm exporting the necessary functions and types from the guardian module—runAuthProbes, reconcileIncidents, the state file path, and the GuardianState type—so the scheduler can import and use them. Then I'll register the scheduler startup in hono-extended so it begins when the server boots, guarded by a global flag to prevent double-initialization.

For the health check verification, I'll run an initial tick immediately on startup rather than waiting for the interval, so the lastHealthAt timestamp populates right away. I'm also adding a guard for the SMS alert on incident open—it'll only send if the SMS provider is ready, otherwise just log it.

Once the backend is deployed and verified, I'll shift focus to the Swift app and build out the guardian view in Command Center while the deploy finishes baking.I'm building the continuous QA scheduler that runs guardian probes on Render at staggered intervals, auto-opens incidents, and sends owner SMS notifications when new incidents trigger.
